current_title: The fleet guide and the push-ACTIVE startup line still present the trust-epoch INCR as the fast revocation path for a --trust key
evidence: Both mechanisms of the claim are closed on the current tree. evidence: When no networked source is supplied the Push tier substitutes `InMemoryInvalidationChannel::new()` and keeps no handle (trust_plane/revocation_resolver.rs:71-75). `new()` initialises `healthy: true` (trust_plane/invalidation_channel.rs:107-112), and `set_healthy` is `pub(super)` and dead outside tests (invalidation_channel.rs:138-143), so `PushInvalidationTrustCache::channel_is_healthy` (trust_plane/push_trust.rs:107-109) reports true forever for a PushInert deployment. The contract has since been rewritten so is_healthy is a WITNESS whose stated value is distinguishing 'no events arrived' from 'nothing could have arrived' (invalidation_channel.rs:62-66) — which is exactly the distinction the inert channel reports wrongly. The honest signal `push_channel_is_inert()` (config_state/trust_revocation.rs:201-203) is still read only for the startup NOTE (trust_plane/mod.rs:265-280). r11 7e0beca7faf43e78 (false-positive) adjudicated a different claim (absent channel read as inert vs refusal), not this value.

current_statement: spawn_trust_reload_task (trust_plane/reload/mod.rs:64-87) registers nothing analogous to TrustEpochSource::require_polling_within (trust_epoch.rs:101-103, 406-413). TrustStoreFreshness (trust_plane/freshness.rs:38-75) is a latch with no last-success timestamp, so a reload loop blocked inside read_trust_file (reload/mod.rs:141) or never scheduled leaves StaleFailsClosed (freshness.rs:88-105) answering from a snapshot that no longer changes, with no fail-closed and no diagnostic. The dropped-unrun and halt-on-first-sleep cases from r10 are closed (managed_worker/mod.rs:139-149; reload/mod.rs:103-118).
current_title: The --trust reload worker has no liveness bound, so a wedged reloader is indistinguishable from a healthy one and the frozen store keeps answering
evidence: Partly closed, core still present. Closed: a body dropped unrun is not reachable — `WorkerSet::spawn` creates the thread immediately and an Err is propagated (managed_worker/mod.rs:139-149) through `spawn_trust_reload_task(...)?` (trust_plane/mod.rs:296-304), aborting materialize; a `Halt::sleep` that returns true now marks the store stale PERMANENTLY (trust_plane/reload/mod.rs:103-118); a panic is converted by the supervisor (trust_plane/reload/supervision.rs:34-51). Still present: `spawn_trust_reload_task` registers no liveness bound (reload/mod.rs:64-87), and `TrustStoreFreshness` is still a pure latch with no timestamp (trust_plane/freshness.rs:38-75) that only the loop writes. A reload body that is alive but wedged — a `read_trust_file` blocked on a hung mount (reload/mod.rs:141, no timeout possible on std::fs), or a starved thread — leaves `is_stale()` false and `StaleFailsClosed` (freshness.rs:88-105) serving the frozen snapshot indefinitely. The sibling epoch source has the bound (`require_polling_within` registered before the body is returned, trust_epoch.rs:401-413; enforced by `polled_recently`, :114-124). No later r11/r12 finding states this defect (r11 a4656205d7bc4c50/ec8bf0e08af41ebf concern the panic supervisor's test, not liveness).

The plane reads `plan.reload().cadence_secs()` at trust_plane/mod.rs:296 and :440, i.e. the witness. A zero cadence is unrepresentable (`NonZeroU64`, trust_plan.rs:30-38). current_statement: TrustStoreFreshness::is_stale (trust_plane/freshness.rs:72-74) loads `terminal` and `stale` with Ordering::Relaxed while every writer uses SeqCst (freshness.rs:50-70); the code states no happens-before edge between Drop's mark_stale_permanently (trust_plane/mod.rs:202) and a concurrent verification's read in StaleFailsClosed (freshness.rs:94). current_title: The trust-freshness fail-closed latch is written SeqCst but read Relaxed on the verification path
evidence: Unchanged in substance, code moved to trust_plane/freshness.rs. `mark_stale`, `mark_stale_permanently` and `mark_fresh` store/load with SeqCst (freshness.rs:50-70) while `is_stale` — the per-verification read on the request path — loads both flags Relaxed and independently (freshness.rs:72-74), consumed by `StaleFailsClosed::resolve` (freshness.rs:94). The analogous Relaxed-vs-SeqCst finding r12 72302b76e5cdc81b was in tls_plane/revocation_currency.rs, a different owner; it does not cover this file.

current_statement: trust_reload_cycle marks the store stale after 5 consecutive failed reads (trust_plane/reload/mod.rs:159-169) and StaleFailsClosed then refuses every verification (trust_plane/freshness.rs:94-102) until a read succeeds. Intended direction; the availability cost of the revocation guarantee is not recorded as an accepted risk.
current_title: Anyone able to make --trust unreadable for 5 cadences takes request verification down on that replica (accepted fail-closed trade)
evidence: The row records an accepted availability trade, not a defect, and it still holds exactly: after TRUST_RELOAD_FAILURE_BUDGET (=5, trust_plane/reload/mod.rs:49) consecutive failed reads `mark_stale()` is set (reload/mod.rs:159-169) and `StaleFailsClosed` returns Unavailable for every (signer, key_id) (trust_plane/freshness.rs:88-105) until a successful read calls `mark_fresh` (reload/mod.rs:141-157; freshness.rs:65-70). Recovery is witnessed by `a_recoverable_staleness_is_undone_by_a_successful_reload` (freshness.rs:112-121). No later finding records it; it should be dispositioned accepted-risk/positive-control rather than fixed.

current_statement: TRUST_RELOAD_FAILURE_BUDGET (trust_plane/reload/mod.rs:49) is fixed at 5 and unrelated to T or tier; layer A's cadence_violations (config_state/trust_revocation.rs:307-340) constrains only R, so the delivered worst case 5R (+T for caching tiers) is never checked against the declared window. The number is now disclosed (delivered_window.rs:43-89; mod.rs:309-314), but the Live guarantee string still leads with 'near-zero' (revocation_tier.rs:152).
current_title: The reload failure budget multiplies R by 5 with no bound against the declared window, so Live's legal worst case is 300s under a 'near-zero' guarantee
evidence: Partly closed. The understatement half is closed by r11 2f9369483620fe25 (fixed): the delivered window now prints budget x R + T (trust_plane/delivered_window.rs:43-89, printed at trust_plane/mod.rs:309-314), and each failed read's WARNING states the extension (trust_plane/reload/mod.rs:171-178). The exposure itself is unchanged: `TRUST_RELOAD_FAILURE_BUDGET = 5` is still a bare constant related to neither T nor tier (reload/mod.rs:39-49); the loop still sleeps a full R before each read (reload/mod.rs:103, 120); and layer A's `cadence_violations` still bounds R alone (`reload <= MAX_NEAR_ZERO` = 60 for Live, `<= min(60, T)` for Push, config_state/trust_revocation.rs:307-340, 423), never budget x R. So a `live` deployment at R=60 has a legal worst case of 300s while its tier guarantee opens with 'near-zero revocation window' (revocation_tier.rs:151-157). The r10 sibling 88873fb4538da56f (accepted-risk, same claim; note: 'flap-reset is an open ruling') is not a later finding, so this row is not closed as a duplicate of it, but an owner may close it by that ruling.
